title: Events Pipeline — Golden Signals
description: SQS → Lambda → DocumentDB, plus the SES email send. Unlike the HTTP services, this one has no http_route or status code: it is a Lambda, and its signals are the per-record lifecycle (app_event) and the email outcome. Its logs arrive through the CloudWatch log group /aws/lambda/3mrai-local-events — the collector's autodiscover must NOT be prefixed to /ecs/ or none of this appears. Email counters also exist as CloudWatch metrics; see the Business Metrics dashboard.

panels.title: Records processed
panels.description: Per-record pipeline outcomes over time. event_processing_succeeded is the healthy path; _failed and _skipped (duplicate) are the two it can end in instead.

queries.query: SELECT histogram(_timestamp) AS x_axis_1, COUNT(*) AS y_axis_1, app_event AS breakdown_1 FROM logs WHERE service_name = 'events-pipeline' AND app_event LIKE 'event_processing_%' GROUP BY x_axis_1, breakdown_1

panels.title: Events by lifecycle stage
panels.description: Every app_event the Lambda emits, ranked. Dominated by the STARTED → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED lifecycle plus the email send; a rising *_failed bar is the signal to look at.

queries.query: SELECT app_event AS x_axis_1, COUNT(*) AS y_axis_1 FROM logs WHERE service_name = 'events-pipeline' AND app_event IS NOT NULL GROUP BY x_axis_1 ORDER BY y_axis_1 DESC

panels.title: Processing latency
panels.description: How long a record takes end to end (insert → handler → COMPLETED), and how long the SES send inside it takes. A p99 climbing while p50 stays flat points at a slow dependency on a subset of records, not a general slowdown.

queries.query: SELECT histogram(_timestamp) AS x_axis_1, approx_percentile_cont(duration_ms, 0.5) AS y_axis_1, approx_percentile_cont(duration_ms, 0.95) AS y_axis_2, approx_percentile_cont(duration_ms, 0.99) AS y_axis_3 FROM logs WHERE service_name = 'events-pipeline' AND duration_ms IS NOT NULL GROUP BY x_axis_1

panels.title: Events by producing actor
panels.description: author_actor names WHO originated each event (users_api:register, tracking_api:carrier_status_update, …), as distinct from the user it is about. Shows which producer drives the pipeline's volume.

queries.query: SELECT author_actor AS x_axis_1, COUNT(*) AS y_axis_1 FROM logs WHERE service_name = 'events-pipeline' AND author_actor IS NOT NULL GROUP BY x_axis_1 ORDER BY y_axis_1 DESC

panels.title: Recent failures
panels.description: Every failed record with its machine-readable reason. A PermanentError is NOT retried — the email is lost — while a TransientError will be redelivered by SQS, so `reason` is what tells the two apart.

queries.query: SELECT _timestamp, app_event, reason, event_id, author_actor FROM logs WHERE service_name = 'events-pipeline' AND (app_event LIKE '%_failed' OR severity_text = 'ERROR') ORDER BY _timestamp DESC
